```{r Huber}
library(broom)
library(patchwork)
library(MASS)

huber_2025 <- data_2025 |> 
  mutate(
    obesity_prop = percent_adults_with_obesity / 100,
    logit_obesity = log(obesity_prop / (1 - obesity_prop))
  )
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(MASS)

# Fit both models
model1 <- rlm(logit_obesity ~ food_environment_index + percent_physically_inactive, data = huber_2025)
model2 <- rlm(logit_obesity ~ percent_physically_inactive + percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods, data = huber_2025)

# Extract and tidy coefficients
coef_df1 <- tidy(model1, conf.int = TRUE) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    model = "Model 1 (Food Env. Index + Inactivity)",
    OR = exp(estimate),
    OR_low = exp(conf.low),
    OR_high = exp(conf.high),
    term = recode(term,
      "food_environment_index" = "Food Environment Index",
      "percent_physically_inactive" = "Physically Inactive (%)")
  )

coef_df2 <- tidy(model2, conf.int = TRUE) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    model = "Model 2 (Inactivity + Food Access)",
    OR = exp(estimate),
    OR_low = exp(conf.low),
    OR_high = exp(conf.high),
    term = recode(term,
      "percent_physically_inactive" = "Physically Inactive (%)",
      "percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods" = "Limited Access to Healthy Foods (%)")
  )

# Combine into one dataframe
combined_coefs <- bind_rows(coef_df1, coef_df2)

# Plot both models together with faceting
ggplot(combined_coefs, aes(x = OR, y = term, color = model)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 3) +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(xmin = OR_low, xmax = OR_high),
    height = 0.2,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Odds Ratio (Effect Size)",
    y = NULL,
    color = "Model",
    title = "Comparing Two Models: Obesity Predictors"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("steelblue", "darkorange")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```



```{r huber table}
library(MASS)
library(broom)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)

# Prepare data
huber_2025 <- data_2025 |> 
  mutate(
    obesity_prop = percent_adults_with_obesity / 100,
    logit_obesity = log(obesity_prop / (1 - obesity_prop))
  )

# Fit models
model1 <- rlm(logit_obesity ~ food_environment_index + percent_physically_inactive, 
              data = huber_2025)
model2 <- rlm(logit_obesity ~ percent_physically_inactive + percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods, 
              data = huber_2025)

# Calculate comparison metrics
comparison_stats <- tibble(
  Model = c("Food Env. Index + Inactivity", "Inactivity + Food Access"),
  R_squared = c(
    1 - (sum(residuals(model1)^2) / sum((huber_2025$logit_obesity - mean(huber_2025$logit_obesity))^2)),
    1 - (sum(residuals(model2)^2) / sum((huber_2025$logit_obesity - mean(huber_2025$logit_obesity))^2))
  ),
  AIC = c(AIC(model1), AIC(model2)),
  BIC = c(BIC(model1), BIC(model2)),
  MAE = c(mean(abs(residuals(model1))), mean(abs(residuals(model2))))
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 3)))

# Print formatted comparison table
kable(comparison_stats, 
      caption = "Huber Regression Model Comparison",
      col.names = c("Model", "R²", "AIC", "BIC", "MAE"),
      align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c"),
      format.args = list(big.mark = ",")) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE,
                position = "center")

# Create and display coefficient plots
p1 <- coef_plot(model1, "Model 1: Food Environment Index + Inactivity")
p2 <- coef_plot(model2, "Model 2: Inactivity + Food Access")

# Create and display residual plot
resid_plot <- ggplot(resid_data, aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(color = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "darkred") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Model Residual Diagnostics", 
       x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Arrange all plots
(p1 + p2) / resid_plot +
  plot_annotation(title = "Huber Regression Model Analysis",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16)))
```

```{r scatterplot}
library(patchwork)

physical_obesity_plot <- data_2025 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = percent_physically_inactive, y = percent_adults_with_obesity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "% Physically Inactive",
    y = "% Adults with Obesity"
  ) 
healthy_plot <- data_2025 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods, y = percent_adults_with_obesity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "% Limited Access to Healthy Foods",
    y = "% Adults with Obesity"
  ) 

food_obesity_plot <- data_2025 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = food_environment_index, y = percent_adults_with_obesity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = "Food Environment Index (0 = worst, 10 = best)",
    y = "% Adults with Obesity"
  ) 
combined_plot <- physical_obesity_plot + healthy_plot + food_obesity_plot 


combined_plot
```

```{r correlation matrix}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(corrplot)
library(ggcorrplot)

# Select relevant variables for correlation analysis
corr_data <- data_2025 %>%
  select(percent_adults_with_obesity,
         percent_physically_inactive,
         percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods,
         food_environment_index,
         median_household_income,
         percent_rural) %>%
  rename(
    "Obesity Rate" = percent_adults_with_obesity,
    "Physical Inactivity" = percent_physically_inactive,
    "Limited Food Access" = percent_limited_access_to_healthy_foods,
    "Food Environment Index" = food_environment_index,
    "Median Income" = median_household_income,
    "Rural Population" = percent_rural
  )

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(corr_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Create correlation plot
corrplot(cor_matrix, 
         method = "color",
         type = "upper",
         tl.col = "black",
         tl.srt = 45,
         addCoef.col = "black",
         number.cex = 0.8,
         diag = FALSE)
```
